title: Docs for your library
description:
Write the documentation for a small library so someone else could use it without reading the code.

```
README: what it is, a 10-line example, building, the API list
ring_buffer.h: a comment on every public function (pre- and postconditions, complexity, errors)
example.cpp: the README's example, compiling and running
```
hints: Write the example first, then the reference: it shows you what a reader needs to know (lesson 5.04).
Doxygen-style comments (`///`, `@param`, `@return`) can be turned into web pages later.
requirements: Use the ring buffer (or any small class) you already wrote in another course; put it in `ring_buffer.h`.
The README example is copied from a file that compiles, so it can never go out of date.
Each function comment answers: what, when it fails, what it costs.
stretch: Generate HTML from the comments with Doxygen on your own machine.
